```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.align = "center", out.width = "96%")
root <- normalizePath(params$project_root, winslash = "/", mustWork = TRUE)
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root)
tab <- file.path(root, "output", "tables")
fig <- file.path(root, "output", "figures")
read_out <- function(file) read.csv(file.path(tab, file), check.names = FALSE)
fmt <- function(x, digits = 2) ifelse(is.na(x), "—", formatC(x, digits = digits, format = "f"))
```

## Overview

This report compares the **Clinical-First (C1)** and **Regulatory-First (C2)** conditions. Questionnaire differences are paired within participant and calculated as **C2 minus C1**. The data contain eight participants and 48 case observations. Given the small sample and unequal case mix, inferential results are exploratory; expertise and order splits are descriptive.

```{r sample}
q <- read_out("questionnaire_paired_comparisons.csv")
t <- read_out("time_on_task_summary.csv")
knitr::kable(data.frame(Participants = max(q$n), Case_observations = sum(t$n), Measures = nrow(q)), caption = "Analysis sample")
```

## Questionnaire scores

SUS uses standard alternating-item scoring and is scaled to 0–100. Adapted NASA-TLX is the unweighted mean of six 1–10 items, with the performance item reversed. TiA subscales use the repository's Koerber item mapping; items 5, 7, 10, 15, and 16 are reverse-scored before computing subscale means.

```{r questionnaire-figure, fig.width=9, fig.height=7}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(fig, "questionnaire_scores.png"))
```

```{r questionnaire-table}
q$C1 <- paste0(fmt(q$C1_mean), " (", fmt(q$C1_sd), ")")
q$C2 <- paste0(fmt(q$C2_mean), " (", fmt(q$C2_sd), ")")
q$Difference <- fmt(q$mean_difference_C2_minus_C1)
q$`95% CI` <- paste0("[", fmt(q$CI95_low), ", ", fmt(q$CI95_high), "]")
q$`Cohen's dz` <- fmt(q$cohens_dz)
q$`Signed-rank p` <- fmt(q$wilcoxon_p, 3)
knitr::kable(q[c("measure", "n", "C1", "C2", "Difference", "95% CI", "Cohen's dz", "Signed-rank p")],
  col.names = c("Measure", "n", "C1 mean (SD)", "C2 mean (SD)", "Mean difference", "95% CI", "Cohen's dz", "Exact signed-rank p"),
  caption = "Paired questionnaire comparisons (C2 minus C1)")
```

Confidence intervals use the paired t distribution. Signed-rank p-values use the exact sign-permutation distribution of midranks, omitting zero differences. No multiplicity correction is applied. Cohen's dz is the mean paired difference divided by the standard deviation of paired differences; rank-biserial effects are also available in the CSV output.

```{r forest, fig.width=9, fig.height=5.5}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(fig, "questionnaire_paired_differences.png"))
```

### Experience groups

```{r groups}
g <- read_out("questionnaire_by_experience.csv")
g$mean <- fmt(g$mean); g$sd <- fmt(g$sd)
knitr::kable(g, col.names = c("Measure", "Experience", "Condition", "n", "Mean", "SD"), caption = "Descriptive scores by experience")
```

## Time on task

Task duration is converted from `h:mm:ss` to seconds. For the paired C1–C2 comparison, case times are averaged within each participant and condition, giving each participant equal weight. Case-level distributions are shown by expertise and by observed block.

```{r time-figure, fig.width=8.2, fig.height=4.8}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(fig, "time_on_task.png"))
```

```{r block-figure, fig.width=8.2, fig.height=4.8}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(fig, "time_by_block.png"))
```

```{r time-tables}
tt <- read_out("time_on_task_summary.csv")
tt$mean_seconds <- fmt(tt$mean_seconds, 1); tt$median_seconds <- fmt(tt$median_seconds, 1); tt$sd_seconds <- fmt(tt$sd_seconds, 1)
knitr::kable(tt[c("condition", "expertise_level", "n", "mean_seconds", "median_seconds", "sd_seconds")],
  col.names = c("Condition", "Experience", "n", "Mean seconds", "Median seconds", "SD seconds"), caption = "Case-level task time")
tp <- read_out("time_on_task_paired_comparison.csv")
knitr::kable(data.frame(n = tp$n, C1_mean = fmt(tp$C1_mean, 1), C2_mean = fmt(tp$C2_mean, 1),
  difference = fmt(tp$mean_difference_C2_minus_C1, 1), CI95 = paste0("[", fmt(tp$CI95_low, 1), ", ", fmt(tp$CI95_high, 1), "]"),
  dz = fmt(tp$cohens_dz), signed_rank_p = fmt(tp$wilcoxon_p, 3)), caption = "Paired participant mean task time (seconds)")
```

## Assistant-participant BI-RADS agreement

Exact agreement requires the same BI-RADS number. Suspicion bands are Low (1–2), Moderate (3–4), and High (5). BI-RADS 0 cannot be assigned to a band, so the output includes both a denominator excluding BI-RADS 0 and a version counting it as a departure. Agreement is descriptive and does not establish diagnostic accuracy against a clinical reference standard.

```{r agreement-figure, fig.width=8.2, fig.height=4.8}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(fig, "birads_agreement.png"))
```

```{r agreement-table}
a <- read_out("birads_agreement_summary.csv")
a$Rate <- paste0(a$agreements, "/", a$n, " (", fmt(100 * a$proportion, 1), "%)")
knitr::kable(a[c("condition", "expertise_level", "measure", "Rate")],
  col.names = c("Condition", "Experience", "Agreement measure", "Agreement"), caption = "Agreement by condition and experience")
```

## Condition order

Block order is inferred from source row order, treating each participant's first three records as block one. Condition-order questionnaire differences and block-time changes are descriptive because each order subgroup is small.

```{r order-tables}
o <- read_out("condition_order_questionnaire_differences.csv")
o$mean_difference <- fmt(o$mean_difference); o$sd <- fmt(o$sd)
knitr::kable(o, col.names = c("Measure", "Condition completed first", "n", "Mean C2–C1", "SD"), caption = "Questionnaire differences by order")
ot <- read_out("condition_order_by_participant.csv")
ot$first_block_mean_seconds <- fmt(ot$first_block_mean_seconds, 1)
ot$second_block_mean_seconds <- fmt(ot$second_block_mean_seconds, 1)
ot$time_change_second_minus_first <- fmt(ot$time_change_second_minus_first, 1)
knitr::kable(ot, col.names = c("Participant", "Experience", "First condition", "First block mean (s)", "Second block mean (s)", "Change (s)"), caption = "Observed order and time per participant")
```

## Interpretation and limitations

The results summarize the supplied records and should not be read as a causal estimate of presentation format. The sample is small, case allocation differs between conditions, and repeated case presentations occur. Treat subgroup and order comparisons as descriptive. All tables and figures are also saved separately under `output/tables/` and `output/figures/`.
